title: Improve date display in thin vertical panels
line: In thin vertical panels, numeric dates like 14/10/2024 now wrap onto several lines instead of shrinking to a tiny font.
explanation: On vertical panels the date label wraps at word boundaries and shrinks its font until it fits the panel width. Numeric dates such as 14/10/2024 or 2024-10-14 contain no spaces, and the line-breaking rules don't allow a break after a slash or hyphen between digits, so the whole date was treated as one word and shrunk to a barely readable size. On vertical panels the clock now inserts an invisible zero-width space after each separator between numbers, so the date wraps there (e.g. 2026- / 11-24) at a normal size when the panel is thin, and stays on one line when there is room.

commits.message:
applets/digital-clock: let numeric dates wrap in vertical panels

Dates like 14/10/2024 or 2024-10-14 have no spaces, so in thin vertical
panels they could not wrap and were shrunk to a tiny font. On vertical
panels, allow line breaks after the separators between their numbers.

BUG: 494736

media.caption: 46 px left panel, zoomed: dd/MM/yyyy date (left) and ISO date (right) are tiny
Same panel with the fix: both dates wrap at their separators at a readable size
Wide (130 px) vertical panel: dates still fit on one line, nothing changes

review.text: The diagnosis of why numeric dates shrink in thin vertical panels is right, and adding break opportunities on vertical panels is a reasonable direction for preserving custom/ISO formats, but the patch has code-quality and UX issues before merging. Most critically, it embeds a literal invisible U+200B character in the QML string literal instead of an explicit \u200B escape, and the regex matches letters rather than just separators. In addition, wrapping dd/MM/yyyy into three lines with dangling slashes directly conflicts with Nate's c2/c8 feedback on the bug report and deserves either a cleaner default vertical format or explicit VDG sign-off.
changes: Replace the raw literal invisible U+200B character inside the replacement string with the explicit escape sequence "$1\u200B" so it is visible in editors, diffs, and GitLab without triggering invisible-Unicode warnings.

Narrow the regex in DigitalClock.qml so it only inserts break opportunities after actual punctuation/date separators (e.g. '/', '-', '.') rather than arbitrary non-whitespace non-digit runs like [^\s\d]+, which mis-wraps formats containing letters such as '2026-W47' or fails to break after '24/' in '24/Nov/2026'.

Re-evaluate the UX for default short dates on thin vertical panels against Nate's c2/c8 comments: consider using a space-separated abbreviated date format (e.g. day + abbreviated month) for the default shortDate on vertical panels instead of wrapping into three lines with dangling slashes ('24/' / '11/' / '2026'), or confirm with VDG that dangling-separator wrapping is acceptable.
